texts.facts: 1. The case of the prosecution is that a complaint was filed by complainant Smt. Santosh w/o Late Sh. Ram Niwas r/o Village Kildaudh, Dist. Jhajjar, Haryana under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C. by raising the allegation against (1) Parvesh @ Monu and (2) Vicky (both sons of Sohan Lal), (3) Sohan Lal and (4) Roshini, all resident of VPO Ujwa, New Delhi and (5) Station House Officer PS Jaffarpur Kalan, New State vs . 1. Parvesh Sharma, on 4 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99651573/ 1 Delhi with request to register FIR against them. She in her said complaint stated that "She married her daughter namely Usha with Parvesh i.e. accused No.1 on 08.12.2004 with great pomp and show after taking loan from near and dear one. She further stated that she had given various articles in the said marriage, out of which most of them were demanded by the accused person. She further stated that on the very next day of the said marriage, all the accused persons had started demanding dowry from the complainant's daughter. For this purpose, Usha was subjected to various physical and mental cruelties by the accused persons and some time, accused Parvesh had left Usha at the complainant's house at Jhajjar. However, the matter was not reported to any police authority with a hope that by the passage of time, every thing will be all right, specifically with accused No. 1 Parvesh and he will accept her daughter. She further stated that within the first year of marriage, accused No. 1-4 had conspired and had thrown Usha from first floor of her matrimonial house at Ujwa, however, she survived and sustained grievous injuries. She further stated that accused persons are greedy and peevish in nature and they never treated Usha as a human being. Number of Panchayats were organized after the incident of throwing Usha. 2. Moreover, Usha had delivered one child at complainant's house as accused Parvesh had left deceased Usha at her house at the time of her delivery with a threat that in case a girl child is born, they will not take her back. Deceased Usha told complainant that accused no.2-3 crossed all the limits of humanity and started making undue and illegal advances and on this, she advised her to discuss this issue with her husband Parvesh. 3. Thereafter, when Usha talked to Parvesh, she was snubbed by accused No.1 and accused No.1-4 told her that "if she will accede to their demands, she will loose nothing but on the contrary she will be accepted as a family member, will enjoy in every manner and that there will be no more dowry demand by the accused persons from Usha" but Usha refused the same. Complainant further stated that thereafter, Usha was treated in inhuman manner and cruel behavior by accused No.1-4. She was not given proper food, cloths etc. They did not allow Usha to come at her parental home or any other relative from her parental side, also not allowed to talk anyone on mobile or telephone and if any person used to call at her matrimonial home, accused No.1-4 used to abuse the said caller and never allowed him/her to talk to Usha. 4. She further stated that on 09.04.2012, there was function at house of Sh. Anil Kumar (brother of Usha) at parental house of deceased Usha for which complainant and Sh. Anil had folded hands and bowed themselves number of times before accused No.1-4. The accused No. 3 and 4 had then told complainant and Anil that Usha can visit the said function with accused No.1 only if the complainant or any other relative gives Rs. 50,000/- to him as compensation price of accused No.1 visiting the said function. The said amount was paid by brother of deceased. She further submitted that accused No. 4 is black magician (Tantrik). She further stated that in the said function, Usha met them last and during her talks with her sister Smt. Sushila, she showed apprehension toward her safety and life because of illegal dowry demand from her father and brother by the accused persons and cruel behavior including merciless beatings by accused persons. But Usha was pacified by complainant and her sister that everything will be alright as the desired amount has been paid to accused No.1. She further stated that on 08.07.2012 at around 7 a.m., accused No.1 made a call to her and Smt. Sushila and informed that Usha has expired because of a heart attack. But some unknown person State vs . 1. Parvesh Sharma, on 4 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99651573/ 2 called from Village Ujwa and informed that Usha had not died with heart attack but she has been murdered by accused no. 1-4. 5. Thereafter, complainant, brother and Sushila and with other relatives rushed to Village Ujwa where a call was made to PCR at 100 number. She further stated that Smt. Sushila filed a written complaint on 08.07.2012, against accused No.5 (who was SHO and not summoned), who had first arrested accused 1-4 but they were let off for some vested interests and thereafter, complainant filed a complaint to ACP Najafgarh, who accepted the same but refused to give receiving, reasons known to him best. It is further stated that no article of specimens were preserved by the police officials for forensic examination, though the PM report seems to be procured. There were other evidences also available at the crime spot against the accused persons but were not collected by police officials. Apart from that complainant and her relatives were not allowed to see Usha's dead body and it was only after the Media was roped in by complainant's relatives that dead body of Usha was shown to the complainant. She further stated it is a common practice that no person of village will stand witness against an accused of his own village. She further stated that because of greedy nature, sub-standard values, illegal act and conduct, accused persons murdered Usha in most ghastly manner. She further stated that due to the said act of the accused persons, a young and charming life has been lost. The accused No.5 and other senior officers did not investigate the matter as per law for the reasons that their palms have been greased and culprits are roaming openly. She further stated that not only this, accused No.1-4 have also issued threats that in case complainant or her any of the family members pursue the matter at higher level or in Court, then the complainant and each and every of her relative shall be eliminated from this world. She further stated that accused No.1-4 are guilt of offences u/s 302/304B/498A/120B/506/34 IPC for which they are liable to be tried and punished as per law. 6. The complainant and Smt. Sushila has also filed a complaint before ACP and DCP but police had failed to take any action. She further stated that police official were trying to show that her daughter Usha had committed suicide instead of taking action against accused No. 1 to 4 and 5. She further stated that she has no option than to approach the Court." 7. Thereafter, on the abovesaid complaint, Sh. Vikram, Ld. MM, Dwarka Courts had ordered to register FIR immediately and investigate the matter and to file the compliance report on 08.08.2012. For the compliance on the abovesaid order, the case was assigned to Insp. Rajesh Dahyia for investigation and during investigation, Insp. During investigation, on 21.07.2013, accused Parvesh Sharma was arrested after taking the permission from ACP/NJF and also statement of witness i.e. complainant, sister and brother of deceased and of villagers were also recorded. 8. After completion of investigation chargesheet was filed under Sections 306/498A IPC against the accused Parvesh Sharma. 9. texts.arguments: 15. Ld. APP argued that the case of the prosecution has been duly proved by the prosecution witnesses and also submitted that PW4 Smt. Santosh, PW5 Smt. Sushila and PW10 Sh. Anil supported the case of the prosecution. They all deposed that about the harassment and cruelty of accused persons and the manner in which deceased Usha was treated by them. There is a demand of Rs. 51,000/- by the accused persons at the time of the function of the son of PW10 Sh. Anil Kumar, which was duly supported by the abovesaid witnesses. 16. The counsel for the accused has submitted that accused Parvesh and deceased Usha were residing separately from other accused persons and living happily. He further stated that there is no demand of dowry at any point of time and accused persons never harassed deceased Usha. He further stated that there are improvements in the testimony of PW2 Smt. Santosh. 17. The counsel for the accused has relied upon the judgment titles as: (I) State vs Jitender Garg & Ors., passed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi dated 21.11.2007 State vs . 1. Parvesh Sharma, on 4 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99651573/ 8 (ii) Sanju @ Sanjay Singh Sengar vs State of Madhya Pradesh, passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court. 18. What the charged offences says: Section 306 IPC says that: "If any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with imprisonment ..............." Section 498A IPC says that: "Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty- Whoever, being the husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty- Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects wuch woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ........................ Explanation- for the purpose of this section "cruelty" means: (a) any willful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand." 19. Reliance has been placed upon by the counsel for the accused on the judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court titled as Baijnath & Ors vs State of Madhay Pradesh, Criminal Appeal No. 1097 of 2016 decided on 18.11.2016, the relevant para 35 wherein it has mentioned that "This Court while often dwelling on the scope and purport of Section 304B of the Code and Section 113B of the Act have propounded that the presumption is contingent on the fact that the prosecution first spell out the ingredients of the offence of Section 304B as in Shindo Alias Sawinder Kaur and another vs State of Punjab- (2011) 11 SCC 517 and echoed in Rajeev Kumar vs State of Haryana-(2013)16 SCC 640. In the latter pronouncement, this Court propounded that one of the essential ingredients of dowry death under Section 304B of the Code is that the accused must have subjected the woman to cruelty in connection with demand for dowry soon before her death and that this ingredient has to be proved by the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt and only then the Court will presume that the accused has committed the offence of dowry State vs . 1. Parvesh Sharma, on 4 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99651573/ 10 death under Section 113B of the Act." The same parameter applied to Section 306 IPC also when the question of abatement of suicide arises due to Section 498A IPC. 22. Reliance is placed upon judgment passed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi titled as State Vs. Paramjeet Singh & Ors.. In the said judgment, the Hon'ble High Court reproduced the observation made by the Apex Court in case titled as Satvir Singh Vs. State of Punjab, (2001) 8 SCC 633, with respect to the phrase "soon before" and same is reproduced herein below:- "It is not enough that harassment or cruelty was caused to the woman with a demand for dowry at some time, if section 304-B is to be invoked. But it should have happened "soon before her death." 23. Counsel for accused persons has further relied upon judgments titled as Umed Singh & Ors. Vs. The State, NCT of Delhi and titled as Naveen Vs. The State, NCT of Delhi decided by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. In said judgment, the Hon'ble High Court has discussed the observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Gangula Mohan Reddy Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh, 2010 (1) SCC 750 which are given below: "In State of West Bengal V. Orilal Jaiswal and Anr. (1994) 1 SCC 73, this court has cautioned that the Court should be extremely careful in assessing the facts and circumstances of each case and the evidence adduced in the trial for the purpose of finding whether the cruelty meted out to the victim had in fact induced her to end the life by committing suicide....." Reliance is placed upon judgment titled Dr. Jhamman Lal Vs. State (Delhi Administration) 2011 [4] JCC 2932 wherein it was held that ".....It is settled law that if a witness makes even two inconsistent statements- Evidence of such a witness cannot be relied upon-No conviction can also be based on such evidence....". It was also held that "......A person cannot be held guilty on mere probabilities-Evidence of witnesses or circumstances surrounding the incident should in a definite tendency and unerringly point towards the guilt of accused......." The counsel for accused has also relied upon judgment titled State of Gujrat Vs. Jayrabhai Punjabhai Varu having Criminal Appeal No. 1236/10 decided by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India wherein in para No. 13 it was held as under:- 13)..... 26. In these circumstances, the judgment relied by the counsel for the accused titled as Sanju @ Sanjay Singh Sengar vs State of Madhya Pradesh, passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court here seems to be right. texts.other_lawyer_arguments: What the charged offences says: Section 306 IPC says that: "If any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with imprisonment ..............." Section 498A IPC says that: "Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty- Whoever, being the husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty- Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects wuch woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ........................ Explanation- for the purpose of this section "cruelty" means: (a) any willful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand." 19. In the latter pronouncement, this Court propounded that one of the essential ingredients of dowry death under Section 304B of the Code is that the accused must have subjected the woman to cruelty in connection with demand for dowry soon before her death and that this ingredient has to be proved by the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt and only then the Court will presume that the accused has committed the offence of dowry State vs . 1. Parvesh Sharma, on 4 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99651573/ 10 death under Section 113B of the Act." The same parameter applied to Section 306 IPC also when the question of abatement of suicide arises due to Section 498A IPC. 22. Reliance is placed upon judgment passed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi titled as State Vs. Paramjeet Singh & Ors.. In the said judgment, the Hon'ble High Court reproduced the observation made by the Apex Court in case titled as Satvir Singh Vs. State of Punjab, (2001) 8 SCC 633, with respect to the phrase "soon before" and same is reproduced herein below:- "It is not enough that harassment or cruelty was caused to the woman with a demand for dowry at some time, if section 304-B is to be invoked. But it should have happened "soon before her death." 23. In said judgment, the Hon'ble High Court has discussed the observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Gangula Mohan Reddy Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh, 2010 (1) SCC 750 which are given below: "In State of West Bengal V. Orilal Jaiswal and Anr. (1994) 1 SCC 73, this court has cautioned that the Court should be extremely careful in assessing the facts and circumstances of each case and the evidence adduced in the trial for the purpose of finding whether the cruelty meted out to the victim had in fact induced her to end the life by committing suicide....." Reliance is placed upon judgment titled Dr. Jhamman Lal Vs. State (Delhi Administration) 2011 [4] JCC 2932 wherein it was held that ".....It is settled law that if a witness makes even two inconsistent statements- Evidence of such a witness cannot be relied upon-No conviction can also be based on such evidence....".
